newsitem.title: USA: Emerging debt ends up, Peru Brady debt accord Mar 7.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt ends up, Peru Brady debt accord Mar 7.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices wound down the New York trading session on a high note with Peru Bradys rebounding in late trade on news that Peru's Brady debt accord will be finalized next month, traders said.
The Peruvian Economy Ministry said on Monday that the formal closing of its Brady plan deals with commercial creditor banks will be on March 7.

In November, the government signed a preliminary Brady bond debt accord with its commerical creditors containing most of the final details for the restructuring of $4.4 billion of principal and interest.

But the formal closing had been delayed due to a disagreement over interest owed. Traders said uncertainty surrounding the close of the deal had weighed down prices, in addition to ongoing concerns over Peru's hostage crisis.
Meanwhile, Peru Bradys traded higher on the news. Peru Flirb WI PEFLIRB=RR bonds gained one point to trade at 57-1/4 and the PDI WI bonds PEPDI=RR rose 1-1/4 at a 63 bid, traders said.
"Peru's had a tremendous day but that's not too surprising," said Richard Siegal, head of fixed income at Santander Investments.

"There had been some uncertainty surrounding the closing of the deal with the focus on the hostage crisis, in addition, to some suggestion that they (Peru) needed funds to close the deal," Siegal added.
In other news Monday, Peru President Alberto Fujimori met with U.S. President Clinton to discuss the handling of the hostage crisis in Lima.
After the meeting, President Fujimori dismissed suggestions of any "peace accord" with Marxist guerillas who have held hostages in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima since December 17.
The exceptions in Monday's session were Ecuador which faces a national strike on February 5 and Bulgaria Bradys.
A general strike by unions planned for Wednesday to protest the government's austerity policies under President Abdala Bucaram is expected to depress brady prices further.
Unions and opposition groups will hold a strike to demand Bucaram's resignation and to protest big price-hikes for public services, such as electricity, telephone charges and public transport.
Ecuador Pars ECPARS=RR were bid off 1/4 at 45-7/8, Ecuador IEB ECIEB=RR traded off 1-1/2 at 87-1/2.
In other news, President Bucaram announced he would change most of his cabinet ministers on Thursday, the day after the planned general strike.
Bulgaria debt was also off with IABs BGFLTH11=RR trading off 1/8 at 49-1/8 while the discount bonds BGFLTH24A=RR were unchanged at a 53-7/8 bid.
